key_insight: Singular-value spectra of equivariant representations provide orientation-invariant fingerprints for identifying structural symmetry and tracking symmetry breaking.
engineering_relevance: SymFP offers a reusable symmetry diagnostic for crystals, molecules and complex assemblies, including local changes that global geometric measures can obscure.
method: Extract singular-value spectra from equivariant representations using an architecture-agnostic framework.
Identify discrete point groups by matching spectra to symmetry-imposed rank templates.
Quantify continuous symmetry breaking through spectral energy beyond target rank constraints, with subgroup-monotonic leakage scores.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports accurate point-group identification and controlled symmetry-breaking tracking across synthetic structures, molecules, coordination complexes and large biological assemblies, without numerical metrics.
watch_item: Practical robustness to noisy coordinates and numerical rank thresholds is not established in the abstract.
paper_title: Spectral symmetry fingerprints in equivariant representations
